w0_rationale: W0 = alpha/2 = 0.025, the usual LORD++ choice. For ~30 tests a night with no rejection the levels run 1.25e-3 (t=1), 2.3e-4 (t=3), 9.1e-5 (t=10), 3.2e-5 (t=30) and spend 0.0037 of the 0.025 wealth, so a night never exhausts it. A larger W0 (up to alpha) raises those levels at most 2x but shrinks the first rejection's reward (alpha - W0); after any rejection the later levels are nearly W0-independent (alpha_30 ~6.5e-5 for W0 in 0.01..0.049). G5's sign-flip p resolves alpha_i/20 at every level, so W0 decides only marginal effects: at n=37 and the loaded-host T_act sigma 0.0376, 80% power needs ~2.4% at t=1 and ~3.0% at t=30.

layout_bias_decision.chosen: (a) T_act as the decision metric, whole-task T as a guardrail
evidence: A/A (3x24 pairs, base vs env-padded rebuild, loaded host): whole-task Delta +1.68% CI [+0.35%, +3.07%] excludes 0, located in Driver startup (spawn->initialize +6.8 ms); T_act +0.78% CI [-0.06%, +1.64%] includes 0.
Same-binary A/A (2x24): whole-task +0.60% CI [-1.0%, +2.2%], T_act +0.10% CI [-0.22%, +0.46%]: no harness or order bias in either metric.

10 independent no-op candidate builds (R7, 24 pairs each, each its own layout): whole-task build deltas mean -0.14%, sd 0.22%, estimated between-build sd 0.13%, 2 of 10 CIs exclude 0 (noop03 -0.62%, noop06 -0.24%); T_act mean -0.03%, sd 0.12%, between-build sd 0.06%, 0 of 10 CIs exclude 0.
T_act sigma_ln is lower in every A/A: 0.0376 vs 0.0592 (loaded), 0.0122 vs 0.0576 (same binary).

Under load, whole-task outliers are Driver start-up stalls (r02: one trace-off pair sd 0.418 whole-task vs 0.014 T_act); every segment-1 wait lies after the first dispatch, so T_act carries the whole effect (R3: T_act Delta -18%, whole-task -10.5%, same ~50 ms).
layout_bias_decision.rejected: (b) randomised layout padding (each arm built twice, builds alternated): doubles G1 build time per candidate (serialized builds already cap screens at ~16/h), turns the build-layout effect into a 2-level random effect that two builds per arm cannot average out, and inflates sigma; the no-op evidence shows the residual T_act layout effect (between-build sd ~0.06%) is far below tau (2%).
